slides.say: In quadrilateral A B C D, angle A is alpha, angle B is a hundred thirty degrees, and angle C is beta. E lies on A B, and D E bisects angle A D C. Which expression equals angle A E D?
at: In quadrilateral A B C D

slides.say: What makes this hard? We have to go through the whole quadrilateral to find angle D, cut it in half, and then work in triangle A E D, all with letters. [short pause] We'll solve it in two different ways, the math way, with algebra, and then by plugging in numbers.
[short pause] Here's the plan on the figure. The four angles of the quadrilateral add up to three hundred sixty degrees, and only angle D is missing.
at: Here's the plan on the figure
The four angles of the quadrilateral

slides.say: D E bisects angle D, so it cuts it into two equal halves.
And x is an angle of triangle A E D, whose angles add up to a hundred eighty. Its other two angles are alpha and half of angle D.
at: And x is an angle of triangle A E D

slides.say: Now the algebra. Angle D plus alpha plus a hundred thirty plus beta is three hundred sixty.
Three hundred sixty minus a hundred thirty is two hundred thirty. So angle D is two hundred thirty, minus alpha, minus beta.
at: Three hundred sixty minus a hundred thirty
So angle D is two hundred thirty

slides.say: Half of two hundred thirty is a hundred fifteen. So each half, angle A D E, is a hundred fifteen, minus half alpha, minus half beta.
In triangle A E D, x is a hundred eighty, minus alpha, minus angle A D E. And angle A D E is a hundred fifteen minus half alpha minus half beta.
Now we open the bracket. The minus in front of it changes every sign inside. So it's minus a hundred fifteen, plus half alpha, plus half beta.
at: So it's minus a hundred fifteen

slides.say: A hundred eighty minus a hundred fifteen is sixty-five. So the number in the answer is sixty-five, and choice numbers two and four are out, because they have a hundred thirty. We got plus half beta, so choice number one is out too. And minus alpha plus half alpha leaves minus half alpha. So x is sixty-five, minus half alpha, plus half beta. Choice number three is our answer.
at: choice numbers two and four are out
because they have a hundred thirty
so choice number one is out too
Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now let's plug in numbers. The right answer has to be true for every alpha and beta that the givens allow. So it must also be true for one example that we choose. We put our numbers into the figure and into the choices.

The figure is not drawn to scale, so we don't read values from it. Let's take alpha a hundred ten and beta eighty, because they're easy to add and to halve. Any other allowed values would work too. We just have to check that they're allowed.
at: Let's take alpha a hundred ten

slides.say: Let's find angle D. The four angles of the quadrilateral add up to three hundred sixty, so we add the three we know. A hundred ten plus a hundred thirty plus eighty is three hundred twenty. Three hundred sixty minus three hundred twenty is forty. Forty is positive, so our numbers are allowed.
at: A hundred ten plus a hundred thirty

slides.say: D E cuts angle D in half, so each half is twenty.

Now let's find x. In triangle A E D, a hundred ten plus twenty is a hundred thirty, and a hundred eighty minus a hundred thirty is fifty. All three angles of the triangle are positive, so x is fifty degrees.
at: and a hundred eighty minus a hundred

slides.say: Now we put alpha a hundred ten and beta eighty into each choice. With these numbers x is fifty, so the right choice has to give fifty. Half alpha is fifty-five, and half beta is forty. Choice number one says sixty-five, plus half alpha, minus half beta. Sixty-five plus fifty-five minus forty is eighty. Not fifty, out. Choice number two says a hundred thirty, plus half alpha, minus half beta. A hundred thirty plus fifty-five minus forty is a hundred forty-five. Out.

Choice number three says sixty-five, minus half alpha, plus half beta. Sixty-five minus fifty-five plus forty is fifty. It matches. But a match alone isn't enough if another choice also matches, so we check the last one too.

Choice number four says a hundred thirty, minus half alpha, plus half beta. A hundred thirty minus fifty-five plus forty is a hundred fifteen. Out. A mismatch rules a choice out right away, and only choice number three matched. So choice number three is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: So choice number three is our answer
